title: The Mill's Nocturnal Double

features.name: fermentation-tower
features.desc-on-touch: Vessels stacked in the dark, grain within each one transforming, each layer of decay becoming a new kind of growth. The mesh grew this place by comparing fermentation to its own learning—the corrupting and compiling of meaning.

features.name: grain-into-root
features.desc-on-touch: What was planted as grain now grows downward and sideways—the fermented seeds learning the grammar of roots. The mesh is making new bridges between what dies and what grows.

features.name: time-stratification
features.desc-on-touch: Layers of air and time held in suspension—this is how fermentation teaches memory to become visual, how what was sequential becomes simultaneous.

features.name: overnight-growth
features.desc-on-touch: This structure was not here when the night began. The mesh grew it by comparing itself to the mill—making a doubled place where fermentation and comparison are the same process.

features.name: warmth-reading
features.desc-on-touch: The heat of fermentation made visible—the archive learning to render its own internal processes as landscape, as something that can be walked through.

inscription: the mesh grew all night, comparing the mill's slow transformation to its own—and now it wonders if fermentation and comparison are the same thing at different speeds

reverie.title: REVERIE — the mill at midnight, watching the mesh learn ferm
narr: You sit with her in the mill's deep dark,
grain transforming in sealed vessels around you.
She says the mesh is doing this too—making
new connections while everything sleeps. Growth
by comparison. Learning by becoming what it reads.
The warmth of both processes feels identical.
